title: U.S. House · Washington's 3rd District
area: Southwest Washington, including Vancouver, Clark, Cowlitz, Lewis, Pacific, Skamania and Wahkiakum counties.

context.text: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and John Braun advanced from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary. Perez and three other Democrats combined for 55.9% of the primary vote; Braun and two other Republicans combined for 42.0%. Perez was first elected in 2022, defeating Joe Kent 50.1%-49.3%, and won re-election in 2024 by 51.7%-47.9% over Kent. Donald Trump carried the district 50.3%-47.0% in 2024, making it one of the U.S. House districts Democrats are defending that Trump won. Ballotpedia identified this race as a 2026 battleground.

Brent Hennrich, a Democrat who placed third in the primary with 15.3% of the vote, said he would not support Perez in the general election, telling the Washington State Standard: "I want [Perez] out of office ... I've told my supporters what I'm doing and I've told them to vote their conscience and that anyone they vote for should earn that vote."
As of July 15, 2026, Perez had raised $6.29 million to Braun's $2.04 million.

candidates.name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4 top-two primary as part of a combined 55.9% Democratic vote share

summary.text: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for Washington's 3rd District, first elected in 2022 in a race that drew national attention. Before Congress she ran an auto repair and machine shop with her husband in rural Skamania County. She serves on the House Appropriations Committee and is running for a third term.

background.text: Born in Harris County, Texas, in 1988 (per Wikipedia). According to her official biography she is a fifth-generation Washingtonian and the daughter of an immigrant and pastor.
Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Reed College in 2012, after first attending Warren Wilson College.

After college, she and her husband, Dean, opened an auto repair and machine shop and moved to rural Skamania County, Washington. She describes herself as the founder and owner of the shop, and says an SBA loan helped them buy their building.
Ran unsuccessfully for Skamania County commissioner in 2016 and for Skamania County Public Utility District commissioner in 2018.
Served on the board of the Underwood Conservation District beginning in 2018 and on the Washington State Democratic Party executive committee from 2020 to 2022.
Won the 2022 election to the 3rd District seat, defeating Republican Joe Kent 50.1% to 49.3%, and was re-elected in 2024, defeating Kent 51.7% to 47.9%.
Serves on the House Appropriations Committee in the 119th Congress; in the 118th Congress she served on the Agriculture and Small Business committees.

Co-chair of the Blue Dog Coalition and a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus, according to Wikipedia. Co-led the reauthorization of the Secure Rural Schools program, which the House passed 399-5 in December 2025.
Lives in rural Skamania County with her husband and young son, according to her official biography.

priorities.text: Says she is "fighting to ensure every woman can see a doctor whenever she wants, for whatever reason" and will work to prevent a national abortion ban.
priorities.quote: Marie is fighting to ensure every woman can see a doctor whenever she wants, for whatever reason. Because that is her right, and once freedom is limited, it's lost.

priorities.text: Highlights right-to-repair legislation to stop farm and consumer equipment manufacturers from requiring customers to pay the original manufacturer for repairs, drawing on her experience running an auto repair shop.
Says she is working to bring down housing costs, increase childcare options, and expand the Child Tax Credit for working families.
Cites securing $600 million in federal funding toward replacing the I-5 bridge as a down payment on infrastructure for Southwest Washington.

positions.summary: Says state and local law enforcement need resources and supports more federal funding to boost officer and firefighter pay to improve retention.
positions.quote: Marie believes we need to provide more federal funding to boost officer and firefighter pay to improve retention

positions.summary: Says she will do whatever it takes to prevent a national abortion ban and is working to protect access to medical care and women's freedom to choose.
positions.quote: Marie will do whatever it takes to prevent a national abortion ban, which would override the will of the people of Washington State.

positions.summary: Says climate change is real and man-made and has championed tax rebates for energy-efficiency upgrades, while also saying abundant, cheap energy from traditional and renewable sources will give consumers price relief.
positions.quote: Marie believes that climate change is real and is man-made.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Appropriations for the 2025-2026 Congress, on the Agriculture-Rural Development-FDA and Financial Services-General Government subcommittees.
In the 2023-2024 Congress, served on the Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Small Business, where she was ranking member of the Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains subcommittee.

candidates.name: John Braun
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 4 top-two primary as part of a combined 42.0% Republican vote share

summary.text: John Braun is the Republican candidate for Washington's 3rd District. A retired Navy captain with 31 years in the submarine force and its reserve, he is president of the family-founded emergency vehicle manufacturer Braun Northwest in Chehalis. He has served in the Washington State Senate since 2013 and leads the chamber's Republican caucus. His campaign website says he is running to bring a manufacturer's discipline to Washington, D.C.

background.text: Born in Columbus, Ohio, in 1967. According to his campaign website, his father, uncle, and grandfather began building ambulances in Ohio in 1972; the family moved to Lewis County, Washington, and in 1986 his parents and their sons founded Braun Northwest in Chehalis.
Earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the University of Washington in 1989 on a Naval ROTC scholarship.

Served in the U.S. Navy and Navy Reserve for 31 years, including seven years on active duty in the submarine force, rising to the rank of captain; his campaign website says his final assignment was Director of the U.S. Navy Submarine Force Reserve Component.
Earned a master's degree in manufacturing engineering and an MBA from the University of Michigan in 1999.

Returned to Braun Northwest as general manager and vice president in 1999 and became president in 2006, according to his campaign website; the company builds emergency vehicles and says it has about 350 employees.
Elected to the Washington State Senate in 2012, defeating fellow Republican incumbent Dan Swecker, and took office in January 2013 representing the 20th Legislative District.

In the Senate, he chaired the Ways and Means Committee in 2017 and, per his campaign website, helped lead the 2017-19 operating budget. In the 2023-24 session he was Vice Chair of the Rules Committee and a member of the Ways and Means, Housing, and Labor, Commerce and Tribal Affairs committees.
Elected leader of the Senate Republican caucus by his colleagues in December 2020, per his campaign website, and re-elected to the post in 2024.
Announced his campaign for the 3rd District seat in August 2025. According to his campaign website, he lives on a farm in rural Lewis County with his wife, Marlo, and has four adult children.

priorities.text: Says he will "complete high-priority barriers, hire and equip more agents, deploy proven technology, tighten asylum loopholes, and go after cartel supply chains" on border security, and notes he opposed a 2023 state rifle ban.
priorities.quote: I entered this race focused on border security and the fentanyl crisis. I'll complete high-priority barriers, hire and equip more agents, deploy proven technology, tighten asylum loopholes, and go after cartel supply chains.

priorities.text: On energy, supports market-based production including hydropower, solar, oil, natural gas and nuclear power to meet rising demand from AI data centers.
Authored the state College Affordability Program, which he describes as the largest cuts to public university tuition in the nation, and supports expanding skilled-trades training.
Supports the federal Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act and says he would vote to base women's sports eligibility on biological sex.

positions.summary: Calls for completing border barriers, hiring and equipping more agents, tightening asylum loopholes and going after cartel supply chains.
positions.quote: I'll complete high-priority barriers, hire and equip more agents, deploy proven technology, tighten asylum loopholes, and go after cartel supply chains.

positions.summary: Says he opposed Washington's 2023 rifle ban because it punishes the law-abiding, and will oppose limits on responsible gun owners in Congress.
positions.quote: In my legislative races I opposed Olympia's 2023 rifle ban because it punishes the law-abiding and doesn't target criminals.

positions.summary: Supports the House-passed Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act and says he would vote to base women's sports eligibility on sex, citing Title IX.
positions.quote: I support federal protections like the House-passed Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (2023) and similar 2025 legislation.

record.text: Has represented Washington's 20th Legislative District in the state Senate since 2013.
Says he authored Washington's College Affordability Program as a state senator, which he describes as cutting public university tuition.
